samples.question: The picture shows a plain background covered with many short grey strokes and four coloured dots: one red, one green, one blue and one orange. Every grey stroke has the same length, the same thickness and the same colour, and the strokes never touch each other or the dots. The strokes are aimed: if a stroke is extended into a full straight line in both directions, that line passes through one single hidden spot, apart from a small wobble of at most twenty-four degrees that is added to each stroke on its own. All the strokes are aimed at the same hidden spot. Exactly one of the four coloured dots is sitting on that spot; the other three dots are far away from it, and they lie on the same circle as it does. Because of the wobble a single stroke is not enough: the spot is the place that fits all of the strokes together best. The colours of the dots, where the dots and strokes are placed, how many strokes there are and how much ink the picture contains carry no information about the answer. Which coloured dot are the grey strokes aimed at? Answer with one of red, green, blue or orange.
